segments.t: When Max promises to set a feast once his grandfather recovers, the sly old man pretends that the doctor gave him only two months left to live today. Completely fooled and heartbroken, Max brings his grandfather a drink and toasts to his long, happy life.
Дед, только не обижайся.
Вот поправишься, я тебе такой стол накрою!
Давай, давай. Когда поправлюсь, накроешь.
Скоро эта шарманка сломается. Недолго осталось.
Сегодня доктор мне сообщил. Два месяца мне осталось.
Я пока бабушке не говорил.
Что конкретно сказал врач? Какой диагноз?
Дед, мы купим лучшее лекарство!
Старый я стал. Вот он тебе и диагноз.
А ты не расстраивайся.
Счастливую жизнь я прожил.
Ну, за тебя и за твою семью!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Дед, только не обижайся.
'Grandpa, only do not take offense.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'grandfather' and finishing on 'be offended'.
Вот поправишься, я тебе такой стол накрою!
'Once you get better, I will set such a table for you!' Notice how Russian expresses 'here' and 'will set' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. the guest answers right away.
Давай, давай. Когда поправлюсь, накроешь.
'Go on, go on. When I recover, you will set it.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'will set'.
Скоро эта шарманка сломается. Недолго осталось.
'Soon this old ticker will break down. Not long is left.' In Russian, the idea of 'soon' flows naturally into 'remained' without extra filler words.
Сегодня доктор мне сообщил. Два месяца мне осталось.
'Today the doctor informed me. I have two months left.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'tonight' and finishing on 'remained'.
Я пока бабушке не говорил.
'I have not told grandma yet.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'told' without extra filler words.
Что конкретно сказал врач? Какой диагноз?
'What specifically did the doctor say? What is the diagnosis?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'what' and finishing on 'diagnosis'.
Дед, мы купим лучшее лекарство!
'Grandpa, we will buy the best medicine!' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'grandfather' and finishing on 'medicine'. the guest answers right away.
Старый я стал. Вот он тебе и диагноз.
'I have grown old. There is your diagnosis.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'old' and finishing on 'diagnosis'.
А ты не расстраивайся.
'And do not get upset.' The negative particle sits right before the verb meaning 'get upset' to negate the statement.
Счастливую жизнь я прожил.
'I have lived a happy life.' Notice how Russian expresses 'happy' and 'lived through' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Ну, за тебя и за твою семью!
'Well, to you and to your family!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'family'. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

And that concludes the grandfather's tall tale in the dining room. Listen for how he claims the doctor gave him two months to live and tells Max not to get upset. See you in the next scene.
